title: Intuitive Topology
byline: V. V. Prasolov · AMS Mathematical World 4 (1995); Universities Press India reprint
note: Short chapters without numbered sections, so each chapter is a leaf here. Summaries are in our own words; the text stays in the PDF.
summary: A short, picture-driven introduction to topology for readers without the formal machinery. It starts with deforming elastic objects and with knots, uses spanning surfaces and a simple diagram invariant to show that the trefoil cannot be untied, and then makes “same shape” precise through homeomorphisms. The second half turns to vector fields: the index of a singular point, the Brouwer fixed-point theorem, why every vector field on a sphere vanishes somewhere, and fixed-point-free and periodic maps. It ends with a tour of two-dimensional surfaces and their classification. Intuition comes first, with proofs sketched where they stay elementary.

chapters.title: Foreword
chapters.summary: Why topology, and why it begins with intuition rather than definitions.

chapters.title: 1  Deformations
chapters.summary: Puzzles about bending and stretching elastic bodies without tearing.

chapters.title: 2  Knots and Links
chapters.summary: Knots and links as closed strings, the trefoil and its mirror image, and link diagrams.

chapters.title: 3  Spans of Knots and Links
chapters.summary: Surfaces whose boundary is a knot (Seifert surfaces), and what they reveal.

chapters.title: 4  A Knot Invariant
chapters.summary: A number computed from knot diagrams that survives deformations, proving the trefoil is knotted.

chapters.title: 5  Homeomorphisms
chapters.summary: Homeomorphism versus deformation (isotopy), with examples of shapes that are the same and different.

chapters.title: 6  Vector Fields on the Plane
chapters.summary: Continuous vector fields, singular points and their index, and the Brouwer fixed-point theorem.

chapters.title: 7  Vector Fields on Two-Dimensional Surfaces
chapters.summary: Vector fields on the sphere and torus; the hairy-ball result and the sum of indices.

chapters.title: 8  Fixed Point Free and Periodic Homeomorphisms
chapters.summary: Maps of surfaces with no fixed points, and maps that repeat after finitely many steps.

chapters.title: 9  Two-Dimensional Surfaces
chapters.summary: Orientable and non-orientable surfaces (Möbius band, Klein bottle), gluing, and the classification of surfaces.
